projectsMeta.headline: Real systems. Real engineering. Real impact.
projectsMeta.intro: Client names are withheld under the confidentiality terms of each engagement. The systems, the scope and the measured results are described exactly as they were.

projects.title: Headless Commerce Migration
projects.context: A legacy ATG platform was holding back release velocity and could not support the front-end experience the brand wanted.
projects.problem: Checkout was the highest-risk part of the migration. It carried payment integrations, fraud verification and order placement, and any regression would be measured directly in lost revenue.
projects.solution: Led backend development for the move to SFCC Headless on Node.js, redesigning checkout backend logic rather than porting it. Payment-instrument and order-placement logic were rebuilt against third-party providers, and fraud verification moved to asynchronous processing so a slow partner could not slow the user down.
contribution: Owned the checkout backend design across the migration
Moved fraud and verification calls off the synchronous user path
Authored order export, OMS and settlement job scripts
projects.secondaryImpact: Checkout latency held steady despite added fraud verification.

projects.title: Commerce Backend Architecture, PLP/PDP Redesign & Payment Integrations
projects.context: The retailer needed dedicated ownership of its core commerce backend, along with a refresh of high-traffic PLP and PDP pages.
projects.problem: Backend architecture, payment integrations, and storefront page performance needed consistent ownership rather than being handled piecemeal.
projects.solution: Took ownership of backend development and architecture for the core commerce solution, implemented secure payment gateway integrations, and redesigned the PLP and PDP interfaces. Also contributed to a buy-now-pay-later proof of concept aimed at improving the checkout experience.
contribution: Owned backend development and architecture for the core commerce solution
Redesigned high-traffic PLP and PDP interfaces
Contributed to a buy-now-pay-later proof of concept
projects.secondaryImpact: Redesigned PLP/PDP interfaces for high-traffic storefront pages.

projects.title: Cart & Checkout Revamp
projects.context: The cart had been extended repeatedly over several seasons and had become the slowest and least predictable part of the storefront.
projects.problem: Fulfilment complexity was the real driver. Multi-shipment, in-store pickup and same-day delivery all had to coexist in one cart without confusing the shopper or the order management system.
projects.solution: Re-architected the cart with custom plugins and tuned platform configuration, then designed and shipped multi-shipment, in-store pickup and same-day delivery as first-class capabilities. PayPal and Klarna were integrated end to end, and automated test suites were added to protect the flow through seasonal releases.
contribution: Re-architected the cart with custom SFCC plugins
Shipped multi-shipment, in-store pickup and same-day delivery
Integrated PayPal and Klarna payment flows end to end
Built automated test suites to catch regressions before release
projects.secondaryImpact: Recognised internally with a delivery award for the revamp.

projects.title: Mobile Commerce Middleware
projects.client: A Middle East lifestyle retail group
projects.context: A native mobile app needed to read from and write to the commerce platform without being coupled to storefront release cycles.
projects.problem: The app team and the commerce team were on different cadences. Without a stable API layer between them, every platform change risked breaking the app.
projects.solution: Designed and built OCAPI and SCAPI based middleware services running in a cloud environment, translating cross-functional business requirements into versioned API contracts. The contract was agreed before implementation, which let the app and the storefront ship independently.
contribution: Designed the API contract between app and commerce platform
Built OCAPI and SCAPI middleware services in a cloud environment
Translated cross-functional requirements into scalable contracts
Reduced rework by resolving integration trade-offs early
projects.secondaryImpact: Mobile and web release cycles decoupled behind a versioned contract.
